title: Thimbleton Warehousing - ops & integration scratchpad
content:
Call notes (2026-03-09) - quick capture:

Attendees: Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood), Marta (Redwood - infra),
         Laura Kim (Thimbleton CTPO), Aaron M (Thimbleton SRE lead), Jay (warehouse ops)

Context / ask:
- Thimbleton runs multi-site refrigerated warehouses; want LLM assistant to triage incoming sensor anomalies and create incident tickets + suggested remediation text for on-floor techs.
- Primary constraint: no PII or PHI leaves their VPC. Need on-prem or VPC-private deployment.
- Must hit 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for short replies (~40-60 tokens) when queried from on-prem edge gateway. Throughput expected ~120 qps during peak (per region).

Customer current infra:
- Edge gateways on site (x86 servers with 1 A100-equivalent GPU each) connecting to central VPC in us-west-2.
- Existing ticket system: Jira self-hosted behind VPN.
- Event stream: Kafka (on their VPC), with sensor messages enriched by internal rules before LLM ingestion.

Important requirements (explicit):
- Data residency: model input must not persist to Redwood-hosted storage. Audit logs allowed but must be pushed to Thimbleton KMS-encrypted S3 in their VPC.
- Model explainability: need token-level attribution for suggestions for compliance review (audit trail).
- Fallback policy: when dedicated capacity saturated, degrade to a smaller local model (on same private cluster) or return canned guidance templates.
- Retries: client enforces idempotency keys; prefer Redwood route-level throttling to avoid duplicate ticket creation.

Gotchas / risks called out on call:
- Wide variance in sequence length: sensor quick status (10 tokens) vs incident summaries (~200 tokens) -> runtime needs good kernel selection and dynamic batching.
- KV cache benefit limited because queries are often unique (per-sensor/time), so batching and request routing matter for cost.
- On-site GPU model variants: their hardware may not support INT8 quant kernels for selected model; need quantization/runtime testing.
- Network egress: they have strict firewall rules; any private control plane traffic needs whitelisting.

Initial rough architecture (sketch in words):
- On-prem Redwood Private control plane (customers manage control plane endpoints inside VPC). Serving runtime runs in Thimbleton k8s cluster (private).
- Edge gateway forwards parsed event to a local inference pod (fast-path) for single-sentence quick answers. For richer summaries, route to central private cluster with higher-memory GPUs.
- Use token-level logging disabled by default; if audit mode enabled, logs are written to an encrypted S3 bucket inside Thimbleton VPC via IAM role.
- Canary rollout: start with 1 warehouse, A/B compare dedicated high-capacity model vs smaller baseline for cost/latency.

Model choices and notes:
- Suggested starting models: quantized Llama2-13B-ish variant for central summarization, and a 7B distilled variant at edge for quick replies. Need to surface model quality numbers on representative prompt set.
- Try Redwood Optimize to run automatic quantization recommendation based on their per-request sequence length distribution.

Performance targets and experiments to run:
- Latency microbench: 40–60 tokens @ p95 <= 350ms on edge GPU; benchmark both with and without batching.
- Throughput stress: synthetic 200 qps for central cluster to validate autoscale and fallback.
- Cost baseline: estimate per-incident token cost (avg 120 tokens) across models and with caching turned off/on.

Privacy/compliance items:
- Confirm legal on what constitutes "sensor metadata" — some IDs are treated as quasi-PII by their compliance team. If so, require client-side redaction step before sending.
- Need KMS integration checklist: HSM support? Their security wants BYOK (bring-your-own-key).

Open questions (capture to follow up):
1. Which warehouses will be in pilot (site names)? Laura to confirm list by 2026-03-16.
2. Can Thimbleton provide a sanitized prompt corpus (100–200 examples) for our model quality eval by 2026-03-20?
3. Which on-site GPU SKU exactly (model/year) — Evan to request hardware inventory.
4. Jira integration: do they want automatic ticket creation or suggested text that humans must approve? (Impacts idempotency and retry semantics).

Action items / next steps:
- Priya: create a short pilot playbook (2 pager) with architecture options + success metrics — due 2026-03-13.
- Evan: schedule infra discovery call with Aaron; collect GPU SKUs and network egress rules — due 2026-03-12 (ASAP).
- Marta: run quick quantization compatibility run with a 7B/13B candidate on an equivalent instance to estimate latency — due 2026-03-18.
- Laura (customer): confirm pilot sites and provide sanitized prompts — due 2026-03-20.
- Create a Confluence page for traceability and add linked artifacts (I started the page ID above).

Notes to self / quick heuristics to try on pilot:
- Prefer continuous batching window short (5–10ms) at edge to keep latency low but still capture small batching benefits.
- Use function-style tool calling to produce structured ticket fields (priority, sensor_id, timestamp, suggested_action) to make downstream automation easier.
- Add a route-based fallback policy: if central model CPU/GPU load > 80% -> divert to edge 7B for summary + mark as "reduced-confidence" in ticket.

Random scribbles / ideas:
- Could precompute sensor-context embeddings for last 10 minutes and pass nearest 3 to prompt to reduce hallucination for repeated alarms. Embedding store can be within VPC.
- Build a small prompt evaluation harness that runs nightly on their sanitized set and pushes regression alerts to Slack channel.

End of scratchpad. Will prune and formalize into pilot playbook.
__notes_for_dataset_team: informal call notes, contains next steps and questions. kept intentionally rough.
